answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to lock a scarce token as collateral, then assigning work through a reputation graph built from repeated, cross-checked transactions. Creating many fake agents multiplies the collateral needed, while coordinated fraud lets honest peers challenge and slash the bonds. An inlet may admit newcomers, but basalt-like stake and a garden of durable relationships make mass identities expensive to grow and easy to prune.
